question: Why can the player attack during Skyway/zipline travel, and why do server Nano movement buffs only update HUD icons?
nativeConsumer: FFOne app action gate, movement controller and protocol-0104 buff ingress
acceptance: Transport ownership blocks Fire1, Nano use and weapon cycle; removing ownership restores actions without a stale visual lock.
Decoded Add/Change/Del buff values change controller attributes without compounding; 60 Hz simulation proves displacement and jump force.
Real development binary builds and starts with production ECS schedule.

hypotheses.claim: Action gate forced MoveMode::None despite authoritative scripted travel.
evidence: primary-managed: cnAvatarAttack.Update returns for nonzero MoveTYPE; cnAvatarThirdPersonMove uses BroomStick, EpZipline, EpRope and EpSlope; native sync_tutorial_action_gate hardcoded None.

hypotheses.rejectedBecause: This slice is a missing runtime consumer; it does not require changing extracted skill data.
hypotheses.claim: Movement buffs are missing because skill table values were reversed incorrectly.
evidence: primary-managed: Status.UpdateSkillBuff consumes packet TimeBuff.iValue directly. Native ingress only forwarded this packet to SkillBuffUiModel.

hypotheses.claim: All active and passive Nano abilities are now implemented.

differences.detail: Buff IDs 1 speed, 3 jump and 8 slow use packet values: Add=1 and Change=3 replace, Del=2 clears; run speed clamps at zero; personal vehicle suppresses jump bonus.
Vehicle table speed override and equipment movement modifiers are separate existing gaps; no new values are invented.

conclusion: Fixed missing scripted-travel action gate and server movement-buff consumption. Four new regressions pass, including deterministic movement simulation. Full-client world smoke completes. The broader Nano ability backlog is still open.

nativeContract.timing: Ingress before NetworkSessionLifecycleSet::Apply completion, projection before LegacyMovementSet::Simulate. Action gate reads current traversal components and transport resource, not later animation presentation.
nativeContract.ownership: MovementBuffs owns numeric server modifiers independently from icon UI. Session reset and PC load clear them. Each player retains unmodified controller base attributes.
nativeContract.authority: No client-side buff expiry or magnitude synthesis. OpenFusion src/Buffs.cpp Buffs::timeBuffUpdate sends the maximum stack magnitude in TimeBuff.iValue (file SHA256 75c0ed3d97427433c15cd998e733d90bb6b05b571e55ab6847cd803ff6d7106c).

verification.result: 103 passed, 4 failed; includes new scripted travel regression
passed; existing unused CameraProjection import warning
600 frames, automatic completion, world/player/HUD visible; no error or panic. Ordinary production schedule smoke, not a live server ability/transport encounter or FPS comparison.

limitations: Live server Nano combat and a ridden Skyway/zipline journey still need interactive acceptance.

Wider tests have five unresolved failures: cyber_combat_command_faces_attacks_and_enters_death_clip (missing fixture content), ordinary_world_weapon_visuals_use_only_validated_bullets_and_hitscan_endpoints, selected_mission_smart_indicator_uses_grant_waypoint_and_npc_radius, task_start_ack_returns_to_exact_close_only_npc_mode, live_buttercup_interaction_opens_and_recovers_the_nano_mission_list. Their expectations were not changed here.
No full passive/active skill, equipment movement modifier, personal vehicle speed, travel scale/position/handle/render or optimization claim.
